derivation_notes: The parent assumed that matured destruction capacity D alone determines catalytic cyclin removal once formed. Here that assumption is relaxed so mature capacity must also be contemporaneously engaged by the active regulator A, implemented as a joint multiplicative occupancy factor in the degradation flux.
change_summary: Cyclin degradation now depends on both matured destruction capacity D and current active regulator A. This creates phase-dependent separation in dC_dt at matched (C,D) states when A and D are out of sync during oscillations.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Once destruction capacity has matured into D, cyclin degradation is independent of the contemporaneous active regulator fraction A except through A's past effect on D.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Even after assembly or maturation of destruction machinery, catalytic substrate processing can still require active regulator engagement, so mature capacity and active engagement jointly determine effective cyclin removal.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when A/(K_degradation_capacity_activation + A) is effectively constant over the observed regime, especially in the active-engagement-saturated limit A >> K_degradation_capacity_activation, so the added factor is absorbed into k_cyclin_degradation.

response_change.parent_relation: Cyclin removal depends only on the matured destruction capacity D, so at any observed (C,D) pair the degradation term has a unique value independent of whether the system is on the rising or falling side of regulator activation.
response_change.child_relation: Cyclin removal will depend jointly on matured capacity D and the instantaneous active regulator fraction A, so equal (C,D) but different A values along the trajectory produce different dC_dt because mature capacity still requires contemporaneous active engagement for full catalytic throughput.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched cyclin and matured-capacity levels, states with higher A show more negative dC_dt than states with lower A; this creates a hysteretic/phase-dependent separation between approach-to-peak and post-peak portions of a pulse that the parent maps to the same value.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when D is intermediate to high and A varies appreciably along the oscillation, especially during activation-relaxation lag where mature capacity persists while A has already declined or is still rising; negligible when A closely tracks D or D remains near zero.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within ordinary oscillatory traces from the stated initial conditions, the same D level is encountered on different phases with different A; training sees modest separation and holdout extends it to stronger pulses where A-D lag is larger.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where active engagement is always saturated or effectively proportional to a constant, so the added A dependence collapses to a fixed factor absorbed into k_cyclin_degradation.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: joint dependence of cyclin proteolysis on matured destruction capacity and contemporaneous active-regulator engagement
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Even after assembly/maturation of destruction machinery, catalytic substrate processing commonly still requires active regulator occupancy or phosphorylation-dependent engagement, so mature capacity and active engagement jointly determine effective cyclin removal.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient correction because the target law changes from a single-valued mapping in (C,D) to a phase-sensitive mapping in (C,D,A), producing separable trajectory branches at matched C and D that cannot be created by globally retuning the parent constants.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Once destruction capacity has matured into D, cyclin degradation is independent of the contemporaneous active regulator fraction A except through A's past effect on D.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Matured destruction capacity D provides potential throughput, but actual cyclin degradation also requires contemporaneous active-regulator engagement through A.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when A/(K_degradation_capacity_activation + A) is effectively constant over the observed regime, especially in the active-engagement-saturated limit A >> K_degradation_capacity_activation, so the extra factor is absorbed into k_cyclin_degradation.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding C and D fixed along sampled oscillatory trajectories, dC_dt becomes more negative for larger A. The effect is visible during phases where the same D is visited while A differs, notably on the rising versus relaxing sides of a cyclin pulse for intermediate or high D.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because the parent target mapping is exactly single-valued in C and D alone. Refitting k_cyclin_degradation, K_cyclin_degradation_saturation, or K_degradation_capacity_activation can only reshape that common surface, not split matched-(C,D) observations into systematically different dC_dt values according to A.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when D is intermediate to high and A varies appreciably along the oscillation, especially during activation-relaxation lag where mature capacity persists while A has already declined or is still rising; negligible when A closely tracks D or D remains near zero.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within ordinary oscillatory traces from the stated initial conditions, the same D level is encountered on different phases with different A; training sees modest separation and holdout extends it to stronger pulses where A-D lag is larger.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where active engagement is always saturated or effectively proportional to a constant, so the added A dependence collapses to a fixed factor absorbed into k_cyclin_degradation.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current target law treats matured destruction capacity D as if it alone determines cyclin proteolysis, omitting the scientifically plausible need for ongoing active-regulator engagement during substrate ubiquitination/processive destruction.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Once destruction capacity has matured into D, cyclin degradation is independent of the contemporaneous active regulator fraction A except through A's past effect on D.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Even after assembly/maturation of destruction machinery, catalytic substrate processing commonly still requires active regulator occupancy or phosphorylation-dependent engagement, so mature capacity and active engagement jointly determine effective cyclin removal.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent scored mapping from observed states is effectively dC_dt=f(C,D): for fixed C and D, all trajectory points have the same predicted cyclin loss, regardless of whether A is high during regulator activation or low during relaxation. A realistic refinement is to relax that single-phase assumption and let active regulator engagement modulate the already matured destruction machinery. The varied condition is oscillation phase along trajectories that revisit similar C and D values while A differs because A activates faster than D matures and later relaxes while D decays more slowly. Holding C and D fixed, the child predicts stronger degradation when A is higher and weaker degradation when A is lower. This is a genuine target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary-trajectory change, because A is already an observed supplied state in the solver contract. The contrast is admissible in the existing scenario for intermediate/high activation where A-D lag exists; if oscillations are too small or A and D nearly coincide, the effect may be weak. A single shared refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce systematic phase splitting at matched (C,D), because its output is single-valued in C and D alone.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make one process depend jointly on two declared quantities.

states.description: Active fraction of the cyclin-degradation regulator

scenario_text: A single-cell regulatory module is followed through several cycles of cyclin accumulation and destruction. Cyclin promotes activation of a degradation regulator, while the activated regulator accelerates cyclin removal and later relaxes back toward inactivity. These coupled intracellular processes can generate repeated cyclin pulses without treating extracellular conditions as dynamic variables. The target is the instantaneous cyclin concentration change along the joint trajectory.
